chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Hasan ibn Abi Uqba al-Sayrafi, from al-Husayn ibn Khalid al-Sayrafi. He said:

I said to Abi al-Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him): A man purifies himself after defecation while wearing a ring on his finger with 'there is no god but Allah' engraved on it. So he said: I consider that disliked for him. I said: May I be your ransom! Did not the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and every one of your forefathers (peace be upon them) do that while their ring was on their finger? He said: Indeed, but they would wear the ring on the right hand. So fear Allah and watch over yourselves.

I said: What was the inscription on the ring of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him)? He said: Why do you not ask me about those who came before him? I said: Then I ask you. He said: The inscription on the ring of Adam (peace be upon him) was: 'There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.' He descended with it.

And when Nuh (peace be upon him) boarded the Ark, Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him: 'O Nuh! If you fear drowning, then proclaim My oneness a thousand times, then ask Me for salvation — I will save you from drowning and those who believe with you.' He said: When Nuh (peace be upon him) and those with him were settled in the Ark and raised the sail, the wind stormed against them. Nuh feared drowning, and the wind rushed him, so he could not proclaim the tahlil a thousand times. So he said in Syriac: 'Haluliya a thousand, a thousand times, O Lord, settle [the waters].' He said: The sail settled and the Ark continued on. So Nuh (peace be upon him) said: 'Surely the words by which Allah saved me from drowning are worthy of never leaving me.' He said: So he engraved on his ring: 'There is no god but Allah, a thousand times; O Lord, rectify me.'

He said: And when Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was placed in the catapult, Jibra'il (peace be upon him) became angry. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him: 'What makes you angry, O Jibra'il?' He said: 'O Lord! Your Friend — there is no one who worships You on the face of the earth besides him — yet You have empowered Your enemy and his enemy against him!' So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed to him: 'Be silent. Only a servant who fears losing [his chance] hurries, like you. As for Me, he is My servant — I take him whenever I will.' He said: So Jibra'il (peace be upon him) was calmed, and he turned to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and said: 'Do you have any need?' He said: 'Not from you, no.' So Allah the Mighty and Majestic then sent down a ring containing six phrases: 'There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, there is no might nor power except by Allah, I have entrusted my affairs to Allah, I have leaned my back on Allah, Allah is sufficient for me.' Allah the Majestic in His Majesty revealed to him: 'Wear this ring, for I shall make the fire cool and peaceful upon you.'

He said: The inscription on the ring of Musa (peace be upon him) was two phrases derived from the Torah: 'Be patient and you will be rewarded; be truthful and you will be saved.' He said: The inscription on the ring of Sulayman (peace be upon him) was: 'Glorified is He who reined in the jinn with His words.' The inscription on the ring of 'Isa (peace be upon him) was two phrases derived from the Gospel: 'Blessed is the servant who remembers Allah for His sake, and woe to the servant who forgets Allah for his own sake.' The inscription on the ring of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) was: 'There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.'

The inscription on the ring of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was: 'Sovereignty belongs to Allah.' The inscription on the ring of al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was: 'Glory belongs to Allah.' The inscription on the ring of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was: 'Surely Allah will accomplish His will.' Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) used to wear the ring of his father al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) used to wear the ring of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). The inscription on the ring of Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) was: 'Allah is my Guardian and my protection from His creation.' The inscription on the ring of Abi al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) was: 'Allah is sufficient for me.'
Al-Husayn ibn Khalid said: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) then spread open his palm — and the ring of his father (peace be upon him) was on his finger — until he showed me the inscription.

key_terms.استنجاء: Ritual purification after defecation — fiqh ruling about wearing sacred inscriptions during this act
key_terms.التهليل: Proclaiming 'la ilaha illallah' — here commanded a thousand times as a protection against drowning
key_terms.المنجنيق: Catapult — the trebuchet used by Nimrod to hurl Ibrahim into the fire
key_terms.حسبي الله: Allah is sufficient for me — the ring inscription of Imam Musa al-Kadhim, also a Quranic phrase (65:3)
key_terms.لا إله إلا الله: The shahada — 'there is no god but Allah', the core of Islamic monotheism
key_terms.لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله: There is no might nor power except by Allah — one of the six phrases on Ibrahim's ring
key_terms.نقش الخاتم: Ring inscription — each Prophet and Imam's ring bore a phrase reflecting their spiritual identity

ai.seo_question: What were the inscriptions on the rings of the Prophets and Imams according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) was asked about the permissibility of wearing a ring inscribed with 'la ilaha illallah' during istinja (purification). He ruled it disliked, noting that while the Prophet and Imams did so, they wore rings on the right hand. This led to a remarkable narration tracing the rings and their inscriptions through all the major Prophets — from Adam through Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Sulayman, and 'Isa — to the Prophet Muhammad and each of the twelve Imams, culminating in Imam al-Rida displaying his father's ring. The historical context is significant: each inscription reflects the spiritual state or mission of that Prophet or Imam, and the chain of ring inheritance among the Imams demonstrates the continuity of Imamate authority.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from Muhammad b `Ali al-Kufi from al-Hasan b. Abi `Uqba al-Sayrafi from al-Husayn b. Khalid al-Sayrafi. He said:

I said to Abi’l Hasan `Ali b. Musa al-Rida (as): [What is the ruling of] a man who purifies himself [after defecation] while wearing a ring on his finger with “there is no god but Allah (la ilaha illallah)” etched on it? So, he said: That would be hateful of him. So, he said: May I be your ransom! Didn’t the Messenger of Allah (s) and every one of your forefathers (as) do that while their ring was on their finger? He said: Of course, but they would wear their ring on the right hand. So, fear Allah and watch yourself.

I said: What was etched on the ring of Amir al-Mu’minin (as)? So, he said: Why do you not ask me about those who came before him? I said: Then I ask [that of] you. He said: On the ring of Adam, it was etched: “there is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (la ilaha illallah, muhammadan rasulullah)”. Habatullah had the same as him.

When Nuh (as) boarded the Ark, Allah revealed to him: “O Nuh! If you fear drowning, then sanctify Me one thousand times, then ask Me to save you, and I will save you from drowning and those who believe in you.” He said: When Nuh (as) and those with him settled on the Ark and he released the rope, the storm wind gusted them, and Nuh feared that he may drown. The wind intensified, but he was unable to sanctify one thousand times. So, he said in Syriac: “Glorify Him a thousand thousand times. O waves, settle (Haluliya alfa alfa, ya mariya atqin).” He said: So, the rope settled, and the Ark continued. So, Nuh (as) said: “Surely, I must not abandon the words by which Allah saved me from drowning.” He said: So, he etched in his ring: “There is no god, one thousand times over. O Lord! Rectify me (la ilaha illallah alfa marra. Ya rabb, islahni).”

He said: When Ibrahim (as) was placed in the furnace, Gabriel (as) became angry. So, Allah revealed to him: “What made you angry, Gabriel?” He said: “O Lord! Your Friend, who is the only servant of Yours who worships You on the face of the Earth, has been overcome by Your enemy and his enemy!” So, Allah revealed to him: “Be quiet. Only a servant who fears death like you would hurry. He is My servant, and I can take him if I wish.” He said: So, Gabriel (as) was relieved, and he turned to Ibrahim (as) and said: "Do you need anything?" So, he said: "From you? No." So, at that moment, Allah descended a ring with six phrases: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, there is no ability nor power except by Allah, I have delegated my matters to Allah, I have relied my back on Allah, and Allah is sufficient for me (la ilaha illallah, Muhammadan rasulullah, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah, fawadtu amri ilalllah, asnadtu thahri ilallah, hasbiallah)." Then, Allah revealed that he should wear this ring, "for I will make the fire cool and peaceful for you."

He said: The etching on the ring of Musa (as) was two phrases taken from the Torah: "Be patient and you will be rewarded, be truthful and you will be saved (asbir tu'jar, asdiq tanaj)." He said: The etching on the ring of Sulayman (as) was: "Glorified is He who reined in the Jinn with His words (subhana man alham al-jinn bikalimatih)." The etching on the ring of `Isa (as) was two phrases taken from the Gospel: "Blessed is the servant who remembers Allah for his own sake, and woe is the servant who forgets Allah for his own sake (tuba li `abdin dhakarallah min ajlihi, wa waylun li `abdin nasiyallah min ajlih)." The etching on the ring of Muhammad (s) was: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (la ilaha illallah, muhammadan rasulullah)."

The etching on the ring of Amir al-Mu'minin (as) was: "Rulership is for Allah (al-mulk lillah)." The etching on the ring of al-Hasan (as) was: "Glory is for Allah (al-`izzatu lillah)." The etching on the ring of al-Husayn (as) was: "Surely, Allah will fulfill His will (innallaha balighu amrih)." `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) would wear the ring of his father al-Husayn (as). Muhammad b. `Ali (as) would wear the ring of al-Husayn (as). The etching on the ring of Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) was: "Allah is my Guardian and my protection from His creation (Allahu waliyi wa `ismati min khalqih)." The etching on the ring of my father Abi'l Hasan Musa b. Ja`far (as) was: "Allah is sufficient for me (hasbiallah)."
Al-Husayn b. Khalid said: Then, Abu'l Hasan al-Rida (as) opened his hand, and he was wearing the ring of his father (as) on his finger, and he showed me the etching.
